pages.text: Long before T. rex, the world had a dinosaur beginning. The Triassic Period started about 251.9 million years ago and came before the Jurassic.
extras: Triassic means the first part of the Mesozoic Era.

images.alt: A map showing Earth during the Late Triassic, about 225 million years ago

pages.text: Back then, the continents were joined in one giant land called Pangaea. Much of it was hot and dry, with wide deserts and big seasonal changes.
extras: One supercontinent, one huge dinosaur stage.

images.alt: A physical map of Pangaea around 230 million years ago

pages.text: The first dinosaurs were not giant monsters. Many were small, quick animals with legs held under their bodies, ready to stand tall and move fast.
extras: Early dinosaurs often walked on two legs.

images.alt: Museum skeletons of early dinosaurs including Herrerasaurus and Eoraptor

pages.text: Meet Eoraptor, one of the earliest-known dinosaurs. It lived in what is now Argentina and was only about as long as a seven-year-old child is tall.
extras: Eoraptor lived about 231 to 228 million years ago.
Its teeth suggest a mixed diet.

images.alt: A size comparison showing Eoraptor beside a human silhouette

pages.text: Fossils are clues from deep time. Eoraptor is known from a nearly complete skeleton, plus other pieces that help scientists rebuild its story.

images.alt: An Eoraptor fossil skeleton preserved in rock

pages.text: Some Triassic dinosaurs were hunters. Herrerasaurus had strong running legs, a balancing tail, and sharp teeth for eating meat.
extras: Herrerasaurus could grow about 6 meters long.

images.alt: A life reconstruction of Herrerasaurus walking on two legs

pages.text: Herrerasaurus looked fierce, but it was still part of an early dinosaur world. Dinosaurs were sharing the land with many other reptiles and mammal relatives.

images.alt: An early dinosaur sharing a Triassic riverbank with a crocodile-line reptile and a small mammal relative

pages.text: Coelophysis was another speedy meat-eater. It lived later in the Triassic in what is now the southwestern United States.
extras: Coelophysis could reach about 3 meters long.

images.alt: A living reconstruction of Coelophysis showing its slender body and long tail beside a human silhouette

pages.text: At Ghost Ranch in New Mexico, scientists found hundreds of Coelophysis skeletons. One quarry became a famous window into Triassic life.
extras: A quarry is a place where rock is dug out.

images.alt: The Coelophysis Quarry area at Ghost Ranch in New Mexico

pages.text: Not every Triassic dinosaur chased prey. Plateosaurus had a long neck, a small head, and leaf-shaped teeth for crushing plants.
extras: Some adults grew up to 10 meters long.

images.alt: A Plateosaurus skeleton showing its long neck, small head, and long body

pages.text: The Triassic ended with a huge extinction. Many reptile groups disappeared, but dinosaurs survived. In the Jurassic, they spread into more places and became the biggest land animals around.
extras: Birds are living dinosaurs, but they evolved later.

images.alt: Dinosaurs surviving from the dark end of the Triassic into a brighter Jurassic landscape
